title: Coordinatewise product law for selector pairs
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\theta\in[-1,1]$. Sample two independent vectors with law $\pi^{\otimes n}$ and, independently at each coordinate, a pair of signs whose first sign is uniform and whose second sign equals the first with probability $(1+\theta)/2$. At each coordinate, use the first sign to select between the two sampled values for the first output and the second sign for the second output. The resulting law on vectors of value pairs equals the product, over coordinates, of the one-coordinate law obtained by this same procedure.
